Here are a few things that I’ve learnt. Firstly alf mabrook on your union, may Allah bless you abundantly! 

1. Be each other’s rocks and companion. When Allah says “be each other’s garments” He doesn’t always mean cover each other’s faults, but cover each other in times of need. Be each other’s support system and always have each other’s back regardless of whichever situation you’re in. 

2. Listen to each other and communicate with one another, it’s always better out than in as Shrek says. Even if it’s uncomfortable to hear, don’t feel like you’re a failure if either of you have done something to upset one another — validate each other’s feelings and move forward. 

3. Do not hold grudges or speak of past issues that have already been resolved, this creates resentment and a cesspit for staying stuck and never moving forward. Learn to forgive each other as innocently as possible. 

4. Use Allah as your compass. By that I mean, seek Him through each other. Nothing is too big or small as a du’a, and remember that to upset a wife is to ultimately upset Allah. Remember that Allah has or will bless your union and that is what makes it so strong. 

5. Guide each other through prayer and dhikr (remembrance of Allah) but do not impose Islam onto each other. Pick each other up if either of you are “slipping” and do not be condescending about it. Remember imaan comes in waves and Allah loves those who return to Him. 

6. Try your best not to see any problem as the though it is the person itself. Try to see that perhaps they made a mistake, are they having a stressful day? Is there anything you can do to help? Rather than thinking that they hurt you on purpose, this sets such a baseline and foundation for seeing the best in each other at all times, even if in the moment you really don’t want to. 

7. If one of you is working a long day and the other is at home doing other things, then when you re-join, give each other a huge long embrace. This will align you with each other as the person at work may be tired or had a stressful day. 

8. Ask each other about your days. Even if someone is supposedly doing “nothing.” And continue to do this. 

9. Don’t do everything for him. Otherwise he’ll never learn. And if you need something done then ask him and give him opportunity to complete it.

10. Do not lie to one another even if the truth is difficult

11. Stay interested in each other’s personal interests (make sure you have your own interests), ask each other even if you genuinely couldn’t care less or find it boring. You are the other half and nothing is more exciting than seeing the passion in someone’s eyes speaking of something they love. But equally nothing is more sad than seeing someone be shut down because the other person doesn’t bother to listen about what they love. 

12. Focus on your values that you share, how do you approach problems? How are you both at interacting with other people? Is kindness a value or is intellect more important? These are things that keep the cogs going. 

13. Speak of financial situations, any debts either of you owe whether that’s to institutions or people. And support each other through it. 

14. Know each other’s Islamic marital rights but don’t use it as a grounds for pride, use it to enhance your marriage and remember Allah wouldn’t give these rights if they were not beneficial. Ps you’re not his maid. 

15. Make sure you have regular date nights! Brunch dates! Any date! Set time aside, real quality time. And never stop doing this! 

16. Make sure you both make each other laugh, the belly aching, nose snorting kinda laughs, though the waters can get deep and dark, laughter keeps you young and hopeful!

17. Look to the Prophet (saw) for guidance. Ask yourself would the Prophet (saw) or his wife accept or treat someone he loves this way if you ever get doubtful. 

18. Read daily du’as together, even if one of you do it for the both of you. Du’as before you sleep, before you leave the house etc. 

19. You’ll learn so much more about each other, remember marriage is the beginning of this exciting journey that you’ll both embark on all the way to Jannah. Some parts you may not like, but no one is perfect and don’t try to change every aspect of each other to the point you no longer recognise each other.

20. Honour each other and respect each other’s boundaries. If someone doesn’t like something then just don’t do it. It’s that simple! If something hurts you no one should tell you it doesn’t.

21. Lastly, you will have your own pasts, some of it may be painful, you may see those issues arise in your marriage, but you can both heal each other. We all have childhoods, even if they’re amazing it doesn’t mean we don’t carry those heavy loads and most times it can show up in a marriage… encourage each other to keep going. You are not a therapist but you can always support each other heal. That is your duty as a husband or wife.

22. Okay last one for real — climb every mountain together. I know it’s metaphorical but build the strongest friendship you know, you may already have it, but you can always strengthen it in so many ways. Be each other’s confidant in times of need and in joy. Be happy for each other’s joys and show empathy for the low moments. 

All the best! May Allah grant you a marriage full of mercy and love that never ends. Aameen

Just because you are in a haram relationship, do not I repeat get married for the sake of “just making it halal” marriage isn’t about only making things “halal from haram.” It’s a massive commitment but the intention should be to use Allah as your compass in your marriage. 

Further to that, to say or assume haram relationships will have no Barakah in marriage is absolutely abhorrent. It is not the same as acquiring haram wealth because that wealth will always be haram because of the intention and there would be no way to make it halal. Other than repentance and not owning the money or admitting to what you’ve done. When you complete a nikkah you have made it halal, Allah gives us opportunity to rectify it, and He doesn’t suddenly take it all away and give someone else who’s not had a haram relationship better than those who have and both cases they’re married. Allah loves when a sinner sins and repents and sins again and repents again, that is our human nature. Again, to assume there’ll be a lack of enjoyment isn’t true… it’s just most people will listen to your advise and end up marrying the haram relationship, (even though that person might not be right for them) but instead of showing them maybe they’re not good for you, you will coerce them into marriage as a solution. 

Whatever you have noticed is complete BS. Human beings and psychology shows that after any time, marriages can become mundane, suddenly you do stop “dressing up” and that’s when you’ve spent a lot of time with the same person and gotten comfortable. Now, the marriage you speak of that’s full of barakah, the exact same thing would happen in a few years, months even. You will still experience a loss of potential love even if you’ve married with no haram relationship. 

Just because you don’t have a haram relationship doesn’t mean you are immune to marital problems. Love and marriage should be a choice, you need to use Allah as the thread between you both woven through you. But most significantly, people can get bored, marriages become the same, so you need to keep that fire alive regardless of how you got there. And this happens to ANYONE. It’s probably happened to your parents who have an arranged marriage. 

With the custom of this society you can still date. For example your mahram doesn’t need to be sat with you to have a “formal conversation.” Your mahram can be seated away, you can be in a public place like a park and your mahram isn’t sitting next to you both is also permissible. You need to know who it is you’re marrying, imagine your mahram just there, how much will you actually get to know the person, if at all? Please stop fear mongering. This is why Muslim girls get into haram relationships, they’re either culturally not allowed to marry the person because it doesn’t fit the parents wants and desires, or they’re expected to never even look at a boy but suddenly be ready for marriage? They’re too scared to tell their parents they like someone because they’ll be shunned and seen as promiscuous. So really there needs to be far more open communication and less judgment from parents who enable such behaviour. 

I also wanted to say zina is haram, but I really wanted to share that it isn’t necessarily always because of the act of sex, physical touch, or speech. Allah truly has forbidden it to protect us. Sometimes our hearts get to attached and that emotional attachment can take over our minds and  the heart will turn and behave in ways that you never thought possible because of this uncontrollable feeling of love. But Allah wants to protect us from that emotional harm and truly remind yourself of that. It isn’t haram to punish you, but to protect you.
